headings.usage: Used for all main titles, player names on table, round announcements, and victory screens to evoke a classic Italian aesthetic.

body.usage: Used for UI controls, chat text, bidding buttons, and stats to maintain modern, highly legible clean interactions.

background.description: Very dark warm wood tone for the app background, simulating an evening in an osteria.

surface.description: Deep bordeaux wood for modals, panels, and waiting rooms.
surface.light_description: Parchment cream for playing card faces.

primary.description: Coppe Red - used for primary actions, CTA buttons, and highlights.

secondary.description: Denari Gold - used for the dealer token, winner highlights, current turn indicators, and the special Re di Denari modal.

visual enhancers.textures: Use subtle noise overlays (mix-blend-overlay with low opacity) on the background to simulate a vintage wooden table. Cards should have a slight parchment grain.
visual enhancers.shadows: Deep, warm ambient shadows (e.g., shadow-[0_8px_32px_rgba(20,10,5,0.6)]) for floating elements like the chat and modals. Playing cards on the table should have crisp drop-shadows.
visual enhancers.borders: 1px solid borders with low opacity gold/wood tones (border-[#D4AF37]/20) for panels to give a premium, authentic feel without overwhelming.

cards.style: Cream/parchment background (`bg-[#F5EBE1]`), rounded corners (`rounded-md`), crisp drop shadow. The back of the cards should use a dark blue or bordeaux intricate pattern.
cards.suits: SVG-based intricate designs for Denari (gold coins), Coppe (red chalices), Spade (blue curved swords), Bastoni (green wooden clubs). Do not use generic poker suits.
cards.interaction: Hover effects should slightly lift the card (`-translate-y-2`) for the player's hand.

bidding_controls.style: A sleek row of buttons appearing above the player's hand during the bidding phase. Use glassmorphism over the Osteria background or solid bordeaux with gold text.
bidding_controls.dealer_constraint: If the player is the dealer and has a constrained choice (cannot declare a number where total tricks == total cards), that button must be visually disabled/crossed out with a tooltip explaining the rule.

seating_layout.style: Elliptical/Radial grid. The local player is ALWAYS fixed at the bottom center (larger avatar and hand). The 2 to 7 opponents are distributed evenly along the top and sides of the screen.
seating_layout.player_avatar: Circular avatar with player name in Cormorant Garamond, trick declaration (e.g., '2/3' won/declared), and an elegant token if they are the current dealer or active turn.

scoreboards.style: Vintage ledger style for the running tournament score. Use a tabular layout with clean Sans numbers. Highlight the current leader in gold.

special_modal.style: When 'Re di Denari' is played, a rich wooden modal slides up requesting the player to choose its value (Nominal vs '0 di Denari'). Use gold accents heavily here to signify its importance.

chat_panel.style: Slide-out or floating panel on the side. Transparent dark background with a blur (`backdrop-blur-md bg-[#1A0F0D]/80`). Clean Manrope text. NO hand log should be printed here.

grids_and_layouts.lobby: Bento-grid layout for 'Create Room', 'Join Room (Code)', and 'Player Stats'. Use large, tactile cards with bordeaux/wood background.
grids_and_layouts.game_table: Dynamic absolute positioning based on circular math to position 3-8 players around a central trick area (`w-full h-full min-h-[70vh] relative`).

motion.cards: Use framer-motion for smooth dealing from the center to players, playing a card to the center trick area, and sweeping the trick to the winner.
motion.turn_indicator: A soft pulsing glow (`animate-pulse`) behind the active player's avatar.
motion.flip: 3D flip animation (`rotateY`) when revealing cards in the final 1-card round.

accessibility.contrast: Ensure all text on dark wood backgrounds meets APCA standards (use cream #F5EBE1 for text).

images.description: Dark brown wooden surface for the table background (use with low opacity or as texture)
Blue intricate playing card back pattern for opponents' cards

3d_libraries.recommendation: Use framer-motion for smooth 2.5D card flips and dealing animations. Full WebGL/Three.js is unnecessary and might make the UI feel less like a tactile 2D card game.

instructions_to_main_agent: Create .js files instead of .tsx (use standard React conventions with PropTypes or JSDoc if needed).
Use standard Tailwind CSS classes. Customize colors in tailwind.config.js to match the provided palette.
Implement WebSocket real-time updates for game state (bidding, playing, chat).
For the SVG Romagnole cards, create separate components for each suit (Denari, Coppe, Spade, Bastoni) to keep the aesthetic authentic. Use appropriate colors for each.
Ensure the game layout scales properly for 3 to 8 players. The math for positioning should distribute players evenly around an ellipse, keeping the bottom center reserved for the local player.
Remember the 'Re di Denari' modal is critical: it must interrupt the flow when played to ask the user for its value.
The final round logic requires showing everyone else's card face-up but keeping the player's own card face-down/hidden to themselves. Implement this specific UI state.
No hand log should be implemented in the chat or anywhere on the screen.
CRITICAL: Do not use complete transparent background in headers, overlays, or any surface that has content under it. Example: Dropdowns and floating chat must have solid or blurred background.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients.
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters (12-24px blur).
You MUST NOT apply universal transition. Eg: `transition: all`. This results in breaking transforms. Always add transitions for specific interactive elements like button, input excluding transforms.
You MUST NOT center align the app container, ie do not add `.App { text-align: center; }` in the css file. This disrupts the human natural reading flow of text.
Always use modern button styles like pill-shaped, or sharp button with interaction animations & color relevant to the app style.
NEVER: use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡🔮🎯 etc for icons.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, parallax effects, and entrance animations. Static = dead.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Subtle grain textures, noise overlays, custom cursors, selection states, and loading animations: separates good from extraordinary.
Main agent relies on these image URLs. Missing categories = main agent will use placeholder text which is FORBIDDEN.
Prioritize using pre-existing components from src/components/ui when applicable.
Use `sonner` for toasts. Sonner component are located in `/app/frontend/src/components/ui/sonner.js` or similar paths.
All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a `data-testid` attribute to facilitate robust automated testing.
